answer: One concrete mechanism: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because echo only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, kernel is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any umber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
